title.narrative: Integrated multisectoral emergency Support for draught and conflict affected communities of Beyeda and Janamora Woredas of north Gonder zone Amhara Region, Ethiopia

description.narrative: ltpgtNorth Gonder is one of the conflict and drought affected areas which people are suffering from the onset conflict between unidentified armed groups and the ENDF. These areas are critically food insecurity that over 20% of the population in Beyeda and Janamora was food insecure by the year 2022. Access to education, health care is their common challenges. Environmental degradation in this area is above national average that leads soil erosion, water scarcity, and loss of biodiversity. The other challenge of this areas are Conflict and displacement that in the year 2022 due to ethnic tension and control of resources, conflict created and over 10,000 people were displaced from the woredas due to conflict ltbrgtThe critical problems facing Beyeda and Janamora woredas are complex and interconnected. Addressing these problems will require a multi-sectoral response such as multipurpose cash support, Nutritional support, WASH Assistance, and Protection. ltbrgtEthiopian Orthodox Tewahido Church Development and Inter-Church Aid commission (EOC-DICAC) has prepared a project entitled as “Integrated multisectoral emergency Support for draught and conflict affected communities of Beyeda and Janamora Woredas of north Gonder zone Amhara Region, Ethiopia ”. The project aims to reduce the impact of humanitarian crises due to drought and conflict at Beyeda and Janamora woredas through providing integrated multispectral life-saving assistance to a target groups.ltbrgtThe project intended to support nutrition, WASH, and MPC services for the most vulnerable community groups in those selected woredas. The services also integrated gender, protection, inclusiveness, accountability to affected people (AAP), and prevention from sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA).ltbrgtMajor Activities Planned included Nutritional support, provision of supplementary food, management of SAM and MAM, strengthening of OTP services, Protection monitoring and vulnerability screening, conduct safety audit, Community based PSS, GBV and PSEA prevention, IEC/SBCC, Local radio spot and public awareness on human right, social cohesion peaceful coexistence under WASH sector Provision of water purification chemicals, WASH NFI, strengthening of WASHCOs and finally provision of MPC for high risk priority groups. Finally capacity building and awareness raising activities are integrated with all sectoral interventions.ltbrgtThese interventions directly contribute for the achievement of the Ethiopian HRP 2023 strategic objectives. These objectives are Reduce morbidity, mortality, and suffering provide protection and safe access to critical, integrated and inclusive basic services and Support vulnerable people to start recovering from crisis and shocks. Stakeholders and partners for the intended project are regional, zonal and woreda level government sectors (DRM, women and social affairs, finance, Water, health ) and FBOs, CBOs, UN relevant Cluster participants, EHF and the OCHA. Delivering services also will be participatory approach that involves the stakeholders and the crises affected peoples. Humanitarian principles such as humanity, impartiality, informed consent, neutrality and independence will be maintained during service delivery and EOC-DICAC staffs will ensure and demonstrate accountability and respect to the rules and regulations of the organization, OCHA, the country and AAP.ltbrgtThe project will be implemented for a period of 8 (Eight) months in Beyeda and Janamora woredas of North Gonder, Amahara Region. ltbrgtThe project will address a total of 6000 Individual communities with budget amounting $600,000 from the Ethiopian Country-based Pooled Fund (CBPF) fulfilling all the operational procedures and guides.ltbrgtlt/pgt
